# Isolde Pembroke

## Overview

- **Age:** Roughly 11 when introduced; turns 13 and later nearly 14 in Brierley.  <sub>[v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c26 P4](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0004), [v1 c30 P6](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0006)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c2 P61](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0061), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021)</sub>
- **Origin:** Pear Hill  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Izzy  <sub>[v3 c29 P10](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Isolde is an attractive girl with black eyes, shiny black ringlets, and rosy, dimpled cheeks. As she gets older, she takes on a matronly look while preserving her dark eyes, red cheeks, and dimples.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v2 c27 P39](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0039), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v4 c1 P2](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0002)_

## Personality

She has a cheerful disposition inherited from her father, along with a good and intelligent nature. Though less prone to extreme imaginative notions than Nell, she enjoys creative play, romantic names, and reading. She possesses a playful side, occasionally engaging in lighthearted pranks, and remains loyal and affectionate to her close companions.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022), [v1 c12 P36](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0036), [v1 c12 P37](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0037), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)_

## Traits

- Good-natured and intelligent  <sub>[v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040)</sub>
- Avid reader  <sub>[v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022), [v3 c11 P30](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0030)</sub>

## Abilities

- Making bookmarkers from tissue paper  <sub>[v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029)</sub>
- Decorative crochet  <sub>[v1 c18 P49](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0049)</sub>

## Goals

- Maintain a lifelong, faithful friendship with Nell  <sub>[v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c18 P50](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0050)</sub>
- Provide her children with pleasant early memories  <sub>[v3 c39 P47](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0047)</sub>

## History

After returning to Pear Hill from Delford, Isolde quickly formed a close friendship with Nell Harcourt, swearing a solemn vow of mutual loyalty above a path pretending to be flowing water. The two girls shared a playhouse named Larkrise and spent their time devising creative titles for local spots. Their companionship suffered a brief setback when Isolde became ill after drinking raspberry cordial at Grey Shutters, leading Mrs. Pembroke to misinterpret the event and temporarily forbid them from seeing each other. The misunderstanding was resolved after Nell rescued Posy Fay, allowing their bond to resume.

During a visit from her grand-aunt Lavinia Pembroke, Isolde and Nell accidentally jumped onto the elderly woman while she was in the spare-room bed, though Nell's earnest apology persuaded Aunt Lavinia to forgive them and fund Isolde's music lessons. As she grew older, Isolde joined the Brierley Village Improvement Society, taking on the role of treasurer. In time, she entered a courtship with Gideon Duckett and eventually married him in a large ceremony at Pear Hill, with Nell serving as her bridesmaid. Later, she gave birth to her first child, a son, followed by a daughter named Small Nell Lucinda.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P8](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0008), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c18 P43](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0043), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c19 P60](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0060), [v1 c19 P83](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0083), [v1 c19 P91](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0091), [v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 c29 P11](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0011), [v3 c28 P23](../source/v03-c28.md#nw-v03-c28-p0023), [v3 c29 P10](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0010), [v3 c29 P11](../source/v03-c29.md#nw-v03-c29-p0011), [v3 c39 P41](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0041), [v4 c1 P2](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0002)_

- Grew up at Pear Hill with her parents, Mr. and Mrs. Pembroke  <sub>[v1 c2 P60](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0060), [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021)</sub>

## Quotes

> Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you.  <sub>[v1 c12 P37](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0037)</sub>

> Following this, Hugh will join your class, and I can assure you that he is accustomed to leading his class. Despite being almost fourteen, he is merely in the fourth book. Four years back, his father fell ill and was forced to travel to Alberta for his well-being, taking Hugh along. Their stay lasted three years, during which Hughie scarcely attended school at all prior to their return. Nell, maintaining your position at the top will not be nearly as simple now.  <sub>[v1 c15 P24](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0024)</sub>

> Aunt Lavinia was the one. Oh, Nell, regardless of how she got to that place, it was Aunt Lavinia. Oh, and her anger is bound to be immense, I am sure. It’s terrible—it truly is terrible—yet Nell, have you ever encountered a thing quite this amusing?  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)</sub>

> Oh, Nell, can’t I assist you in preparing the meal? You are aware that I am able to create wonderful lettuce salad.  <sub>[v2 c16 P25](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0025)</sub>

> I am so eager for the time when he is big enough to speak. Hearing him call me ‘mother’ is my deepest desire. And oh, I am resolved that he will have a pleasant first recollection of me. My own earliest remembrance of my mother involves her striking me because of an act I had committed. I have no doubt that I merited the punishment, and my mother was invariably wonderful and holds a special place in my heart. Even so, I truly wish that my initial memory concerning her had been more agreeable.  <sub>[v3 c39 P47](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0047)</sub>
